draft.title: The basic economic problem
card: People's wants have no end. When one want is met, new ones soon appear.
Resources are limited. There is only so much land, labour and equipment to make goods and services. This shortage is called scarcity.
Wants are unlimited but resources are scarce. This is the basic economic problem.
Because of this, individuals, businesses and governments must choose how to use their limited resources. Choosing one use means going without others.
draft.remember: Unlimited wants meet scarce resources, so choices must be made.

a.q: Why can no society meet all of its people's wants?
opts: Wants are unlimited but resources are scarce
Resources are unlimited but wants are scarce
People only want things they cannot afford
Governments choose not to produce enough
a.why: Wants keep growing, while land, labour and equipment are limited. That gap is the basic economic problem. It is not that wants are scarce, because people always want more.
a.clue: Think about which side has no end and which side runs out.

b.q: Mia's town council in Bendigo has a set budget. It wants a new pool, a bigger library and more bike paths. What does this show?
opts: Limited resources force the council to choose
The council has too few wants to plan well
Scarcity only affects businesses and families
The council can fund every project it wants
b.why: The budget is limited but the wants are many, so the council must choose how to use its money. Scarcity affects governments as well as individuals and businesses.
b.clue: Can the council pay for everything on its list?

a.best: Wants are unlimited but resources are scarce

b.best: Limited resources force the council to choose
